name: Title 1
text: Project Objectives

name: Content Placeholder 2
text:
The following are the Finalized objectives of the project:
1. To develop a BLE-based mobile communication backbone for transmitting real-time patient vitals to a mobile application, which securely forwards data to the cloud using MQTT over TLS, with CoAP as a backup.
2. To integrate the existing patient health monitoring system with the mobile communication backbone for continuous vital acquisition, transmission, and remote monitoring during ambulance transit.
3. To implement RTOS-based concurrent task management for sensor acquisition, vital processing, communication, and local display, ensuring responsive and reliable operation.
4. To develop an ML-based patient risk prediction module that analyses real-time vitals, identifies potential deterioration, and classifies patient risk levels for early clinical assessment.

name: Title 1
text: Wi-Fi vs BLE: Design Rationale

name: Footer Placeholder 3
text: Dept. of Electronics and Communication Engineering, NMIT, Bengaluru

name: BLE fits the phone gateway design. Phone prox
text: BLE fits the phone gateway design. Phone proximity remains a requirement.

preview: Criterion | Earlier Wi-Fi approach | Selected BLE approach

text:
Design rationale, not measured Wi-Fi versus BLE test results. The earlier project README describes direct ESP32 Wi-Fi MQTT/TLS upload. The current architecture moves internet upload, GPS and planned buffering to the phone, while BLE carries nearby vital observations. Wi-Fi also supports local communication without internet, and a phone hotspot can provide a Wi-Fi uplink. The selected design removes Wi-Fi credentials and cloud connection handling from the ESP32 local link; it does not establish better latency, reliability, range or measured power consumption. BLE is designed for low-power point-to-point data exchange, including health monitoring. A fair empirical comparison would use the same board, workload, distance and observation duration, recording current draw, delivery ratio, update interval and recovery time. Sources: https://www.bluetooth.com/learn-about-bluetooth/topology-options/ ; https://www.bluetooth.com/bluetooth-le-primer/ ; https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-idf/en/latest/esp32/api-reference/bluetooth/bt_le.html ; earlier project README at D:/Academ/Projects/Major Project 2026-27/Coding Part/Smart Ambulance/README.md.

name: Conclusion and future work bullets
text:
Implemented ESP32 BLE communication and a Flutter app for simulated vitals.
Supported device discovery, encrypted connection and start/stop control.
Integrate physical sensors, OLED and the full RTOS task pipeline.
Add persistent uploads, cloud services and the hospital dashboard.
Develop GPS tracking, ETA estimation and ML risk prediction.

Conclusions distinguish implemented code from demonstrated hardware results. The full system remains a prototype. ML risk assessment is a project objective and requires dataset/model selection and evaluation.
